description: The line plot illustrates the MRR@10 performance of different DPR-based retrieval models as a function of the number of queries used during inference (S), ranging from 1 to 10 on a linear x-axis. The y-axis, labeled “MRR@10”, spans from 33.0 to 36.5, also on a linear scale, with major tick marks at 0.5 intervals. Six distinct strategies are compared, each represented by a colored line with corresponding markers and line styles: “DPR w/o query” (black solid, no markers) remains flat near 34.0; “DPR w/ gold” (yellow solid with circle markers) starts near 33.0 at S=1 and rises steadily to ~34.8 at S=10; “DPR w/ top-1” (green solid with circle markers) begins at ~34.8 at S=2 and climbs sharply to ~36.4 at S=10; “DPR w/ bottom-1” (purple solid with circle markers) starts near 34.8 at S=2 and increases slightly to ~35.2 at S=10; “DPR w/ random” (blue solid with circle markers) begins near 34.8 at S=2 and plateaus around 35.7 at S=10; and “DPR w/ curriculum” (red solid with circle markers) starts at ~35.6 at S=1 and rises to ~36.0 at S=10. Dotted lines of matching colors represent the same models evaluated without corpus expansion, showing consistently lower performance: “DPR w/ gold” (yellow dotted) stays near 34.8; “DPR w/ top-1” (green dotted) hovers around 35.5; “DPR w/ bottom-1” (purple dotted) remains near 34.8; “DPR w/ random” (blue dotted) is steady at ~35.6; and “DPR w/ curriculum” (red dotted) stabilizes near 35.5. The “DPR w/o query” model has no dotted counterpart. All solid lines show performance gains with increasing S, while dotted lines remain relatively flat, indicating that corpus expansion contributes significantly to performance improvement.
caption_used: Comparison of different query selection strategies. During training, we first expand the document with a query selected from the generated queries using a specific strategy, and then train DPR with the expanded document. During inference, we evaluate the well-trained DPR retrievers with corpus expansion (solid lines) and the typical representation (dotted lines) on the dev set of MS-Marco, where the solid and dotted lines with the same color are results for the same DPR. Notably, the 'DPR w/ bottom-1' strategy demonstrates a consistent increase in MRR@10, reaching approximately 35.2 at S=10, surpassing the 'DPR w/ random' strategy. Additionally, the 'DPR w/ gold' strategy shows a slower rate of improvement compared to 'DPR w/ top-1', stabilizing at around 34.8 by S=10. The 'DPR w/ curriculum' strategy consistently exceeds the performance of 'DPR w/ random' across all query counts, with a peak MRR@10 of approximately 36.0 at S=10.
